(1) THE BUY BUTTON IS LIT AND DEAD: public.hr_unlock_offers carries all four character_slot rows with refusal='namespace_unsupported:character_slot' and gold=null, because a hero slot is priced in GEMS and that generated catalogue has a gold column and no other - so hr_unlock_buy refuses the namespace by construction and the click dead-ends through a confirm modal with no visible outcome. The only other path, src/multi-character.js unlockSlot(), is a client-side `G.gems -= cost`, and gems are SERVER-OF-RECORD and ARMED (src/net/record.js SERVER_OF_RECORD carries `gems` with no dormant gate), so that debit is reconciled away by the next envelope. (2) OWNERSHIP IS CLIENT-AUTHORED in the G.heroSlotsUnlocked residue - the b371 gem dupe that multi-character.js's own header documents ('a cloud restore reverted the gems debit and KEPT the slot - the purchase became free') and whose closing paragraph names this exact verb as the fix. (3) THE ONE FOUND HERE, AND THE BIGGEST: hr_create_character(p_slot) is granted to `authenticated` and has only ever validated p_slot for SHAPE ('if v_slot < 0 or v_slot > 5 then bad_slot'), so POST /rpc/hr_create_character {"p_slot":4} from any signed-in console mints a fifth character with a full starting kit - 500 gold, a Bronze Sword, farm plots, the free Auto-Eat I - for nothing, five times over. That is the entire 3,100-gem ladder bypassed by one fetch, and it would also LAUNDER into a permanent entitlement through this file's own grandfather clause. A price is not a price if the thing can be taken without paying it, so the gate is not scope creep; it is the other half of the same property and lands in the same transaction. WHAT IT ADDS: public.hr_hero_slots (slot_id 1-4, cost_gems, premium_waived; RLS on, no policy, every client grant revoked), public.hr_hero_slots_of(uuid) - the ONE ownership predicate, read by three callers so a grandfather clause cannot have three spellings - and hr_buy_hero_slot__ungated(int,int,uuid) behind a rate-gated authenticated-only wrapper. THE ACCOUNT/CHARACTER SPLIT IS THE DESIGN DECISION: the MONEY comes from the CALLING character's player_state row (the wallet the topbar gem chip is showing - measured on production, the one two-character account holds 527 gems on slot 0 and 0 on slot 1, so charging any other row would take gems the player cannot see and quote a shortfall that is not on their screen), while the ENTITLEMENT is written to the account's canonical row, SLOT 0, and read account-wide (player_progress has no account-level home and an FK onto player_state; filing it under the calling slot would make a slot bought on Hero 2 invisible from Hero 1). Two advisory locks in canonical order - slot 0's key FIRST, byte-identical to hr_apply's - because a per-character lock alone would let two characters of one account buy the same slot at once and both charge. THERE IS NO FREE PATH IN THE VERB: the Hearth Hall waiver moves out of device-local localStorage (one devtools line = three free slots today) and becomes a fact about OWNERSHIP, so a waived slot answers already_owned and never runs a zero-gem grant; the migration's own gate asserts the single grant is downstream of the single debit. Refuses by name: bad_slot / unknown_slot / requires_previous_slot / already_owned / insufficient_gems / no_character / no_account / hero_slot_daily_cap / rate_limited, plus slot_not_owned from the create gate (which src/net/character.js already routes through its `default: refused` branch, so no client change is needed for it to fail safely). MUST RUN AFTER 2026-09-03-intent-mismatch-class.sql - the body calls hr_intent_replay from birth rather than being retro-patched, because player_intents is ONE key namespace for every verb - and AFTER 2026-09-04-auto-eat-at-creation.sql, which is the hr_create_character body Sec 8 anchors into. GRANDFATHERING IS LOAD-BEARING AND MEASURED: production carries ZERO character_slot flag rows and one account (0a47ba77) with characters on slots 0 AND 1, so hr_hero_slots_of counts an existing player_state row as ownership - without that clause the projection would evict a real player's second hero on its first envelope. The clause is safe going forward precisely because Sec 8 makes a row above slot 0 impossible to create without owning the slot. COST AT 100x PLAYERS: four slots exist and each is once-per-ACCOUNT forever, so the lifetime ceiling is 4 player_progress + 4 player_ledger + 4 player_intents rows per account - under 7,200 rows at 600 players, FOREVER, and realistically two orders of magnitude less. hr_hero_slots_of is two index lookups plus a four-row catalogue scan, called once per hr_state_of.
